intro: Start with the first small exercise, or open a database below and explore. The first five stops introduce everyday work; the rest are optional. Allow roughly 10–15 minutes for a first look and take as much time as you like to try things. All examples are fictional and yours to change.
version: Tour data version: 2026-09-11. Dates belong to the day this vault was created. Template updates apply only to future new vaults; this vault is never updated or supplemented from a template.
emptyProjectBody: An empty example for your own next step. No tasks are linked yet: the count is 0 and planned minutes stay blank until there is an effort value.
journalPast: Sample reflection: I kept one useful next step and left room for a break.
journalFuture: Sample plan: leave time for one focused task. This is a plan, not a record of completed work.
journalToday: What would make today useful? Write one sentence, then choose a small task.
reviewBody: Fictional example for review: we will read together for 30 minutes. The format is still a draft; the old date below deliberately asks for a fresh check.
standaloneBody: A quiet space for a new idea. This note intentionally has no links yet. Find it in the graph with isolated notes enabled, then connect it to something relevant.
cheatExtra:
## Small building blocks

- A short list
  - A nested point

```text
A code block keeps *these marks* literal.
```

A [link to this heading](#small-building-blocks) stays inside this note. Try the slash menu on an empty line for more blocks.

steps.title: Write and link
steps.action: Add one sentence to the note, then type [[ and link another example. On the phone, use the edit button first; on the desktop use the editor mode in the toolbar.
steps.result: Your sentence is saved as Markdown. Open the link and look at Backlinks to find the route back.
steps.extra: Use the cheat sheet to try a callout, a nested list, a table, a formula, a Mermaid diagram or a footnote. Compare reading, editing and source modes. Try an image width such as ![[Attachments/skizze.svg|240]]; choose the real attachment path in your vault.

steps.title: Turn a note into a task
steps.action: Find the checkbox in today's note in Tasks → From notes. Choose Move to the task database (database icon; on the phone open the row actions). Open the new task and set its project property to the first example project.
steps.result: The original checkbox becomes a link. The task has its own note and appears in the task database and the project's related tasks.
steps.extra: Set a due date and priority. Change status or check the task off: the checkbox and status stay consistent. A repeating task creates its next occurrence only when completed. The main exercise needs no account.

steps.title: Plan a project
steps.action: Open the first linked task from the project's task list and mark it done. Return to the project table and look at Open tasks and Done (%).
steps.result: The board, table and Markdown describe the same task. Project totals are calculated from related task notes; they are not editable values in the project file.
steps.extra: The task database is embedded in two projects and automatically shows each project's tasks. Try adding a task inside an embed. Explore the timeline: bars have start and end dates; the final review is a milestone without an end. Waits for connects the steps, and the Connections view shows the project and task relations. Effort is in minutes; actual time stays unmeasured until you connect a calendar and block time in stop 09.

steps.title: Find and organize
steps.action: Open Configure → Filters and select a color stripe to find a smaller group of notes. Clear that rule afterwards to return to the full source.
steps.result: A filter changes the visible set, not the files. Available values still come from the whole source, even when a combination has no matches.
steps.extra: Try an icon, whole-note tags or the Labels pinboard view. Tags include the text and frontmatter; labels name the view's configured property. Combine rules with AND or OR. In Properties, show a column, then choose its Summary beneath its name. A total uses only the visible results. Switch to a table to read it; pinning and moving cards remain available in the pinboard.

steps.title: Plan a day
steps.action: Open today's daily note from the calendar or journal database and add a short plan. Follow its previous or next day link.
steps.result: Seven sample days surround the creation date. Past days contain reflections and future days contain plans. A daily note remains an ordinary Markdown file.
steps.extra: The daily-note template keeps its date and neighboring-day tokens for future notes. Try the journal's calendar and table views or show a database as a calendar overlay. Real appointments require a calendar account on desktop; mobile can also use the experimental device calendar with permission. Connect only if useful, as described in stop 09.

steps.title: Review a note
steps.action: Select a sentence and add a comment to yourself. On desktop it appears alongside the note; on the phone open the comments sheet from the note actions.
steps.result: The comment points at the passage without becoming part of its Markdown. It is a real comment created by you; no conversation is preloaded.
steps.extra: Propose a replacement in the same thread, then accept or reject it. Accepting changes the note; rejecting keeps the text. Resolve the thread when finished or create a task from an actionable comment. Use Open comments to find it again. Other people and cross-device conversations require a connected service; the self-review works locally.

steps.title: Compare versions and keep files
steps.action: After the edit in stop 01, make another small change and save. Open Version history from the note menu and compare the older text. With the default interval, wait at least two minutes between saved changes so a second snapshot can be created.
steps.result: History records real edits on this device. Nothing is fabricated by the template; if no older snapshot exists yet, create one through the exercise first.
steps.extra: Try restoring into a copy before replacing a note. Explore backup retention and export in Settings; an export gives you files to keep elsewhere. Share or export the synthetic import sample linked in stop 09 to make it available to the system file picker. No restore, export or deletion runs automatically.

steps.title: Explore what helps you
steps.action: Search for the title of an example project. Open a result at its matching passage, then inspect its backlinks or local graph.
steps.result: Search and links give you different routes to the same notes. Choose the route that fits how you remember your work.
steps.extra: Try the global graph and enable isolated notes to find the unlinked idea. Create a meeting from the unassigned note template and answer its prompts. Inspect Trust & provenance on the draft reading-evening note and mark it reviewed yourself. Try bookmarks, tabs, split views, the command palette and a different theme. These are independent options, not a checklist to finish.

steps.title: Accounts, devices and import
steps.action: Optional: export or share the linked tour-import.json to a folder the file picker can access. Open Import from another app (desktop: command palette; phone: Settings → Maintenance), select the Simplenote file and import into a new subfolder named Tour import. Check the preview before starting.
steps.result: The synthetic package contains exactly two notes tagged tour-import and no deleted notes. The report should show two imported notes; the existing tour files remain separate. Delete only that new subfolder if you want to undo the exercise.
steps.extra: For sync, connect a demo cloud folder in Settings → Accounts and use a second device to verify one real edit. Configure a calendar before trying appointments or time blocks; a database calendar alone is not an appointment account. Mail capture needs a mail account and a chosen sample message. Login secrets, device permissions and successful sync cannot come from a template. Follow the linked handbook guides; nothing connects automatically.

steps.title: Sharing and automation
steps.action: Optional: read the linked guide and decide whether a shared workflow would help. You can finish the tour here without setting anything up.
steps.result: Notes, tasks and local reviews already work without external accounts. Sharing, encryption and automation become useful when you have a concrete recipient, device or task.
steps.extra: Encrypted workspaces and their sharing flows are experimental and require real identities, keys and a connected service. Use separate demo data to explore roles, invitations and publications. Automation and scripts require deliberate setup and permissions; the template never starts a script, contacts a service, creates credentials or pretends to grant access. Choose one small workflow from the handbook when you need it.
